rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to capture all 8 compounds without truncation and map the overall elution window. This gives a strong first read on whether peaks are unretained, bunched in a narrow phi range, or still eluting near the hold.

All peaks eluted within a narrow effective solvent window, roughly phi 0.20–0.46, so trimming the gradient around that region should spend the run where the peaks are and improve the unresolved 4/5 pair. Keeping tG and T fixed isolates the effect of narrowing the phi window on selectivity and spacing.

The narrow-window run created an extra coelution, so broad-window selectivity is better; now test whether the critical pair is slope-responsive by doubling tG while keeping phi window and temperature fixed. If the 4/5 pair improves substantially, we can later shorten from there; if not, we will pivot to temperature/selectivity changes.

The 4/5 pair is strongly slope-responsive: at 40 min all pairs are resolved, so now shorten from 40 min toward the shortest broad-window gradient that still keeps every pair at or above 1.5. A 24 min test should stay under the 10 min last-peak target while showing whether full resolution is retained.

Resolution of the critical 4/5 pair improves sharply with longer tG, so bracket the minimum gradient time for full resolution between 24 and 40 min. A 32 min run should indicate whether we can achieve all pairs at or above 1.5 while reducing the time penalty versus 40 min.

At 40 min and 40 C all pairs are resolved but the run is too long; the 32 min result also shows a late pair can become critical, so now use temperature to shorten retention and shift selectivity while keeping the proven broad, shallow gradient. This tests whether a higher T can preserve full resolution from the 40 min method while pulling t_last closer to 10 min.

Raising temperature hurt selectivity badly, so test the opposite direction from the fully resolved 40 min method. A modest drop to 35 C may keep all pairs resolved while slightly improving selectivity and helping identify whether temperature can be used at all around the optimum.

Temperature changes were unfavorable, so return to 40 C and keep the successful 20 min slope while trimming only the high-organic end to shift late-eluting selectivity without compressing the whole window as severely as injection 2. Since all peaks in injection 1 eluted by about phi 0.40, lowering phi1 should mainly reshape spacing among the later peaks and may relieve the 4/5 coelution.

Broad-window gradients are clearly best, and the critical 4/5 pair improves monotonically with longer tG, while 20 min is the current best score. A small step to 22 min is the most efficient next test to see whether we can gain enough resolution on 4/5 with only a minimal time penalty and potentially surpass the current best CRF.

The 4/5 pair remains the only serious problem and is not improved by a tiny tG increase, so probe selectivity with a gentler trim of the upper phi limit than before. Since all peaks elute well below phi 0.5, reducing phi1 from 0.95 to 0.90 may subtly reposition the critical middle pair while keeping the overall run close to the current best conditions.

No 20–24 min broad-window variant has fixed the 4/5 pair, while 40 min at 40 C does; the remaining lever is a combined compromise of moderate slope reduction with a small temperature increase to pull t_last back. This tests whether 45 C can shorten a near-resolving long gradient without the severe selectivity loss seen at 50 C.

The 28 min, 45 C run suggests moderate tG redistributes the critical regions, but temperature introduced new weak pairs; isolate the slope effect by running the same tG at 40 C. This will show whether 28 min at the original selectivity is a viable compromise between the unresolved 24 min run and the slow fully resolved 40 min run.

The broad-window optimum still appears near 20 min for CRF, but the nonmonotonic pair behavior between 24, 28, 32, and 40 min suggests a crossover region worth mapping more finely. A 26 min run will clarify whether there is a local selectivity sweet spot between 24 and 28 min that improves the weakest pair enough without too much time penalty.

The unresolved pair at 26–28 min improves substantially versus 20–24 min, and 45 C at 28 min changed which region was weakest, indicating useful selectivity leverage despite some loss. Testing 30 min at 45 C probes whether a slightly shallower gradient can recover both weak pairs while keeping t_last near 12 min, a potentially better compromise than the 40 min fully resolved run.

At 30 min and 45 C both weak pairs are close to acceptable, but temperature still hurts selectivity relative to 40 C in this system. Running 30 min at 40 C should reveal whether this tG is a near-optimal compromise on the original selectivity surface and whether it outperforms the 28 and 32 min runs.

The 30 min, 45 C run is the closest compromise so far, with both weak pairs near 1.5 and better balance than the 40 C runs around 28–32 min. A slightly shallower gradient at the same temperature may bring both borderline pairs over the threshold while keeping the time penalty lower than the 40 min fully resolved method.

At 45 C, increasing tG from 30 to 34 min improved the late pair and left only the 3/4 pair slightly short, so a further small increase is the cleanest way to test for full or near-full resolution on that selectivity surface. This should show whether 45 C has a practical optimum below the 40 min broad gradient.

Longer gradients and temperature adjustments have not beaten the original method, but 45 C clearly changes selectivity enough to shift the critical pair identities. A short 20 min run at 45 C is the missing key experiment to see whether higher temperature can improve the time-efficient method’s resolution pattern enough to exceed the current best CRF.

The 20 min, 45 C run is now best and only two adjacent pairs are slightly below full credit, so the next move is a minimal slope reduction while keeping the favorable selectivity. A 22 min gradient should improve the 3/4 and 6/7 pairs with only a very small risk of adding time penalty, making it the most likely route to a higher CRF.

At 45 C the 20 min broad gradient is best, and increasing tG made the late pair worse, so the next lever is a small reduction of the high-organic limit to reshape selectivity while preserving the short run. Since all compounds elute well before the end of the programmed window, trimming phi1 slightly may improve the two near-critical pairs without introducing a time penalty.

A small trim of phi1 kept the short run but did not beat the best method; one more step lower tests whether the 45 C selectivity surface has a sharper optimum in the upper-phi limit. All compounds still elute far below the program end, so phi1 = 0.85 should remain safe while probing whether either near-critical pair opens further.

The best method is still 20 min at 45 C, and trimming phi1 or lengthening tG only worsened the limiting pairs. With few injections left, test a shorter gradient to see if the same near-critical resolution can be maintained while reducing run time further; if not, injection 18 remains the final choice.

The 18 min, 45 C run improved CRF by reducing total time while leaving only one pair below full credit, so the best remaining opportunity is to see if we can compress further without losing too much resolution. A 16 min test directly checks whether the time savings outweigh any small drop in the already isolated 3/4 pair.

CRF peaked at 18 min and only fell slightly at 16 min, so one more step shorter is worthwhile to map the time–resolution tradeoff near the apparent optimum. If the isolated 3/4 pair remains close to its current value, the faster run could still match or surpass the best score.

The optimum is clearly around 18 min at 45 C, with only the 3/4 pair limiting; the final shot is a small temperature increase from that best slope to see if selectivity for that pair improves while the run remains very short. We already know 50 C is harmful at 40 min, but near the 18 min optimum it is the last unexplored lever with real upside.
